title: 25 AI Prompts for Total Beginners
subtitle: Copy, paste, and adapt. Works with ChatGPT, Gemini, or any chat AI.

sections.name: Everyday writing
prompts: Rewrite this email so it sounds friendly but professional. Keep it under 120 words: [paste your email].
Help me reply to this message. I want to say no politely without burning the bridge: [paste message].
Turn these rough notes into a clear, well-structured message: [paste notes].
Proofread this for spelling, grammar, and clarity. Show me the corrected version, then list what you changed: [paste text].
Give me three subject lines for an email about [topic]. Make one plain, one curious, and one direct.

sections.name: Planning your day and week
prompts: I have these tasks today: [list]. Help me order them from most to least important and suggest a realistic schedule.
Break this big goal into small, doable steps I can start this week: [goal].
Act as a planning partner. Ask me 3 questions to understand my week, then build me a simple plan.
Help me write a short weekly review: what went well, what didn't, and one thing to try next week. Here are my notes: [notes].
I keep procrastinating on [task]. Suggest 3 small first steps that take under 10 minutes each.

sections.name: Learning faster
prompts: Explain [topic] to me like I'm a complete beginner. Use a simple everyday example.
I read this and didn't fully get it. Explain it more simply and tell me the one key idea: [paste text].
Quiz me with 5 easy questions on [topic], one at a time, and tell me if I'm right after each answer.
Give me a 5-day plan to learn the basics of [topic], with one small task per day.
What are the 3 most common beginner mistakes with [topic], and how do I avoid them?

sections.name: Getting real answers, not vague ones
prompts: Before you answer, ask me any questions you need to give a genuinely useful response. My question is: [question].
Give me the short answer first in one sentence, then a longer explanation underneath.
Compare [option A] and [option B] for someone who cares most about [what matters to you]. Use a simple table.
You gave a general answer. Make it specific to my situation: [describe your situation].
List the pros and cons of [decision], then tell me which you'd lean toward and why.

sections.name: Getting things done
prompts: Help me draft a simple checklist for [task or event] so I don't forget anything.
Summarize this long text into 5 bullet points a busy person could read in 30 seconds: [paste text].
I need to make a decision about [topic]. Walk me through it by asking one question at a time.
Turn this idea into a short, clear plan I could hand to someone else: [describe idea].
Act as a friendly coach. I want to build the habit of [habit]. Give me a simple starting plan and one way to stay on track.

footer: A note on using AI well: treat these as starting points, not magic. Always read what the AI gives you, check anything important, and make it your own. — Let Me Teach You AI
